newsitem.title: CHINA: INTERVIEW - Copper trade up on Shenzhen exchange - chief.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Copper trade up on Shenzhen exchange - chief.

text.p: The volume of copper and aluminium traded on the Shenzhen Mercantile Exchange has jumped sharply this year on lower copper prices and increased hedging in aluminium, the exchange's president said on Monday.
"The traded volume in copper between January and April 1997 was 52.2 billion yuan (US$6.3 billion), up 53 percent compared to the same period last year," Zheng Yuanheng told Reuters in an interview.
"The copper price was lower, so there was incentive to use it and domestic investors increased their transactions in copper," he said.
"In January to April 1997, the copper volume was 1,420,000 tonnes, compared to 1,160,000 tonnes in the same period last year," he added.
"For aluminium, the traded amount between January and April 1997 was 1,230,000 tonnes, compared to 240,000 tonnes in January to April in 1996," Zheng said.
The jump was partly attributable to Chinese factories increasing their hedging programs as they better understood the benefits of hedging, Zheng noted.
"If they think the copper price is dropping, they can sell it at a future contract to guarantee their income," he said.
Copper and aluminium were the main contracts traded on the exchange and had been the most successful in the China market.
Speculators had also used market fluctuations to buy and sell, Zheng said.
"Although in 1997 the copper and aluminium prices have not changed a lot, the fluctuations have been quite heavy, so speculators have come in and out of the market," he said.
Last year, the traded volume in metals was relatively low as people preferred to trade coffee and green beans. This year, more people have shifted to copper and aluminium, he said.
Zheng said he was not worried about speculators overrunning the market as China had put in place measures to dampen speculation.
"We see a healthy future for the exchange as commodities markets continue to grow," Zheng noted.
The Shenzhen Mercantile Exchange trades base metals, grain, sugar, diesel fuel and treasury contracts, providing a market place for spot, forward and futures contracts.
Its total business turnover in 1996 was 147.59 billion yuan ($17.8 billion), a dip of 38 percent from 1995.
